title: Cascade-induced high-performance nonreciprocal quantum batteries
abstract: Nonreciprocal quantum batteries harness reservoir engineering for controlled energy transfer, heralding a paradigm shift for quantum energy storage. A prior study utilizing the Metelmann-Clerk formalism reported a fourfold enhancement in nonreciprocal energy accumulation over reciprocal counterparts. This fourfold enhancement, however, appears to stem from a Lindblad master equation that exhibits fundamental inconsistencies, which may systematically understate the actual nonreciprocal advantage. Our approach is rooted in the rigorously established cascaded open quantum systems formalism, which ensures both mathematical consistency and physical fidelity. Remarkably, we surpass the previously reported fourfold benchmark, attaining a regime-independent sixteenfold steady-state nonreciprocal energy advantage over reciprocal systems. We further uncover a dissipation-dependent battery-to-charger efficiency, fourfold under symmetric damping, surpassing this benchmark when the battery is less dissipative, and lower otherwise. This work establishes the cascaded formalism as a mathematically rigorous and experimentally viable foundation for high-performance quantum energy storage.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes nonreciprocal quantum batteries using the cascaded open quantum systems formalism. The authors demonstrate that this method yields a sixteen-fold steady-state energy advantage, significantly surpassing previous theoretical benchmarks. It establishes the cascaded formalism as the mathematically sound foundation for designing high-performance quantum energy storage devices.
main_problem: To develop a mathematically rigorous and physically consistent framework for achieving high-performance nonreciprocal energy transfer in quantum batteries.
main_result: The authors surpassed a previous fourfold benchmark, achieving a regime-independent sixteen-fold steady-state nonreciprocal energy advantage over reciprocal quantum systems.
method: The study utilizes the rigorously established cascaded open quantum systems formalism to model the energy dynamics, contrasting it with flawed prior methods.
model_or_system: The system models a quantum battery coupled to a charger, represented by two single-mode harmonic oscillators, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Energy Storage Capacity ($E_b(t)$) and Useful Work Capacity (Ergotropy, $W_b(t)$), as well as the energy efficiency ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Damping rates ($\kappa_a, \kappa_b$), coupling strengths, and the ratio of dissipation rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Born-Markov approximation, and the primary focus is on establishing the mathematical rigor of the cascaded formalism.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the Cascaded QB model; Figure 2 shows energy efficiency vs. time for different damping conditions; Figure 3 compares nonreciprocal vs. reciprocal energy efficiency.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QB model and the need for a rigorous formalism, develops the dynamics using the cascaded approach, compares results against flawed prior methods (Metelmann-Clerk), and concludes by establishing the superior performance and mathematical validity of the cascaded formalism.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles open quantum systems dynamics, specifically energy flow and dissipation engineering, which are core topics in quantum optics and AMO physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of the Cascaded QB model. The charger and battery are single-mode harmonic oscillators with fre- quencies ωa and ωb and local decay rates κa and κb, respec- tively. The charger is driven by a coherent laser of ampli- tude A and frequency ω0. The reservoir engineering induces a direct coupling √κaκb between the two systems, leading to unidirectional flow of energy from the charger to the battery.

Figure 3. Energy efficiency (nonreciprocal-to-reciprocal stored energy ratio) versus rescaled time τ of the QB system. The system’s parameters are κa = 0.2ω, κb = 0.01ω (blue bold); κa = κb = 0.01ω (black dashed); κa = 0.01ω, κb = 0.2ω (red dotted-dashed); and Ω≈0 (green dotted-dashed). To enable a fair comparison, the coupling strength is set to √κaκb for reciprocal configurations.

Figure 2. Energy efficiency (battery-to-charger energy ratio) of the nonreciprocal QB system as a function of rescaled time τ. The system’s parameters are κa = 0.02ω, κb = 0.01ω (blue bold); κa = κb (black dashed); and κa = 0.01ω, κb = 0.02ω (red dotted-dashed).
